correctness.rationale: For each b>=2, independent Gaussian sketches on diag(I_b,0) give first-lookahead probability 1-F_{b²}(b*tau²); conditional on this, the QR spans the exact range, the next residual is exactly zero, and b independent projected row squared norms have chi-square_b/b law. The algorithm removes a row iff their minimum is below tau². Every such removal causes true squared residual at least one, proving the exact product law. Stirling, endpoint Laplace asymptotics and concentration of the first block prove the sharp c=2 transition and centered Gumbel window. A standalone numerical reproducer reconstructs QR/pruning and independently checks finite distributions; numerical tests do not certify the asymptotic proof.

Historical QB, LU interpolation and HSS stopping studies use distinct coefficient or aggregate stopping criteria. Classical chi-square extreme-value theory is an acknowledged ingredient, not itself claimed novel. Priority remains subject to more comprehensive historical comparison.

value.rationale: The exact finite-block probability and sharp c=2/Gumbel phase expose a genuine risk of below-tolerance rank selection: as block size grows, more unbiased row estimates are minimized, and failure can tend to one despite each estimate becoming more concentrated. This precisely localizes when Gaussian adjoint-free rank pruning needs confidence adjustment on a natural finite-rank flat-spectrum system.
